title: X-Men '97 Season 2 Set for July Premiere on Disney+ with Nine-Episode Run
text:
Disney+ has revealed the premiere date and episode structure for X-Men '97 Season 2. The new season will debut on July 1, 2026, with three episodes, followed by a weekly release of the remaining six episodes over seven weeks, ending on August 12. The storyline continues directly from the first season's finale, scattering the X-Men across multiple timelines-ancient Egypt in 3000 BC and a dystopian future in 3960 AD-as they confront the villain Apocalypse. Episode titles suggest adaptations of famous comic arcs like "Days of Future Past." The original voice cast returns, including Cal Dodd, Lenore Zann, and Alison Sealy-Smith. A new trailer showcases intense mutant action and apocalyptic scenarios.
Disney+ has announced the details for the upcoming second season of X-Men '97 , with the premiere set for July 1, 2026, on the streaming platform.
The season will launch with a three-episode premiere before transitioning to a weekly release schedule. Unlike the first season's 10 episodes, Season 2 will consist of nine episodes spread across seven weeks, concluding on August 12, 2026. The released episode titles hint at major comic book arcs and the possible return of iconic characters. Among the titles are Episode 3: "Rise of Apocalypse - Part 1" (July 1) and Episode 7: "Strange Land, Savage Heart" (July 29).
The narrative picks up immediately after the first season's finale, scattering the X-Men across different timelines-past, present, and future. Trailers reveal Professor X, Rogue, Nightcrawler, Beast, and Magneto confronting the ancient villain Apocalypse in 3000 BC Egypt, where he is known as En Sabah Nur, the first mutant. Simultaneously, Wolverine, Cyclops, Jean Grey, Morph, and Storm face a dictatorial version of Apocalypse in the year 3960 AD.
Episode titles such as "Days of Past Future" strongly suggest an adaptation of the classic "Days of Future Past" storyline from The Uncanny X-Men comics, exploring both a dark future and ancient past. The season will feature the return of original voice actors including Cal Dodd (Wolverine), Lenore Zann (Rogue), Alison Sealy-Smith (Storm), George Buza (Beast), Christopher Britton (Professor X), and Adrian Hough (Nightcrawler).
This continuation aims to blend nostalgic elements with new storylines, expanding the X-Men universe in animated form.
Alongside the X-Men '97 updates, several other entertainment news items were noted, including a plot update for a Matt Damon and Daniels collaboration film, casting news for The Angry Birds Movie 3, a theatrical re-release of Avengers: Endgame under a new title ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, progress on James Gunn's DC Universe following the 2025 Superman film, a production update for the Five Nights at Freddy's 3 movie, a release date setting for Helluva Boss Season 3 on Prime Video, a teaser trailer reveal for Sakamoto Days Season 2 on Netflix, Marvel's new variant covers featuring X-Men icons from the 1980s, and a fresh trailer for X-Men '97 Season 2 highlighting mutant mayhem and apocalyptic action.
These additional items, however, are separate from the core X-Men '97 announcement and serve as broader industry updates
